newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade slips 1.2 pct in Jan-Feb yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade slips 1.2 pct in Jan-Feb yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's trade with China slid 1.2 percent to US$3.178 billion for January and February from the same 1996 period, the Board of Foreign Trade said on Monday.
Taiwan's trade with China represented about 9.1 percent of the island's total foreign trade, the board said in a statement.
Exports to China totalled US$2.619 billion in the January-February period, down 2.9 percent from a year ago and accounting for 14.5 percent of Taiwan's total exports.
The board attributed the export decline to decreasing machinery and textile products.
Imports from China were at $559 million, rising 7.6 percent and accounting for 3.3 percent of the total imports.

The board attributed the import growth to the government's continued opening of goods imported from the mainland and the island's steady rises in industrial output, which pushed up demands for mainland semi-finished goods and raw material.
For January and February, Taiwan enjoyed a $2.06 billion trade surplus with China, falling 5.4 percent from 1996.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
More than 30,000 Taiwanese businesses have operations in China, with investment totalling more than $30 billion since political tensions started to ease in the late 1980s.
